## On routing — thinking out loud while you test
Your layout is a better shape than what exists now, and most of it is cheap. But there's one thing I'd want to resolve before any of it, because it's load-bearing for "running multiple yamls/pulls at a time."

Global temp tables are instance-wide, not connection-private. ##JVM_Patients is visible to every session on the Cosmos instance — the ## is what makes it global. Two concurrent pulls that both produce a cohort named Patients will collide, and my generated SQL opens with DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ##JVM_Patients. Pull B would drop pull A's table mid-run. A would then fail confusingly, or worse, transfer partial rows.

Nothing about per-project folders fixes that, because the collision is in SQL Server's namespace, not the filesystem. The fix is namespacing the temp name — ##JVM_<project>_<dest>, or a short session token. It's contained (naming.py plus the contract), but it's a change to an invariant we've been treating as fixed, so I'd rather raise it than quietly alter it. Worth checking on the VM while you're there: run two sessions concurrently and see whether they interfere.

On the layout itself, three observations:

One root, fixed shape, beats a routing table. You said changing paths before was a pain — I'd read that as too many knobs, not too few. If project_folder is the single input and everything else is derived, there's one thing to set and nothing to keep consistent. Overrides can come later if a specific path genuinely needs to move.

The SneakPeek/Cosmos parquet split is already derivable. Under cosmos_db: Dual, cohorts come out as X and X_sp — so routing parquets into parquets/SneakPeek/ and parquets/Cosmos/ needs no new configuration, just the suffix we already emit. And your instinct to export SneakPeek parquets as soon as those cohorts finish fits the manifest model well: session status already tells you when a variant is complete.

Two things in your sketch are Phase 10 and don't exist yet — contents.yaml and load_parquets.py. Worth keeping them in the layout so the shape is right, but they're not blockers for testing.

The cheap part is the naming: Manifest.yaml instead of pullmanifest.yaml, server/yamls/ instead of split/sessions/, server/sql/ grouped by session rather than flat. Paths inside the manifest are already relative to the manifest, so moving it doesn't break anything.

Go test the delivery — I'd rather hear what breaks on real Cosmos than design more layout on top of untested plumbing.
